title: Benchmark-driven Models for Energy Analysis and Attribution of GPU-Accelerated Supercomputing
problem: GPU energy consumption opaque; coarse-grained metrics insufficient. Developers, architects, practitioners lack granular understanding of energy attribution (functional unit, memory level, control vs datapath), limiting power-constrained optimization and procurement decisions.
motivation: Power constraints increasingly primary limiter in supercomputing. Energy-efficient algorithm and architecture innovation requires understanding where GPUs consume energy (FPU vs tensor core vs memory). Granular energy models enable targeted optimization.
method: We created a reusable energy model by running small diagnostic programs (microbenchmarks) on GPUs to measure exactly where energy is consumed. The model breaks down energy use by specific hardware components (floating-point units, tensor cores, integer arithmetic units), memory tiers (L1 cache, L2 cache, and HBM high-bandwidth memory), and separates energy spent on control logic from energy spent on actual computation. We tested this approach across four GPU generations and validated it against real supercomputing and AI workloads.
key_novelty: The key idea is using small test programs to measure GPU energy in fine detail—identifying which specific hardware component (floating-point unit, tensor core, or integer arithmetic unit), which memory tier (L1, L2, or HBM high-bandwidth memory), and whether it's for control logic or computation—in a way that extends to new GPU generations.
contributions: Granular energy attribution model: functional unit, memory level, control/datapath
Validation on supercomputing and ML/AI workloads
Actionable insights for optimization, procurement, architecture research
limitations: Limited to NVIDIA GPUs (AMD, other vendors not covered)
Microbenchmark representativeness for real applications unclear
Extrapolation to future generations not discussed
Absolute energy values (Joules/operation) not specified in abstract
primary_theme: Fine-grained GPU energy attribution via microbenchmarking
